transcript:
Speaker A (AI): Hello, what is your name?
Speaker B (Human): My name is Zara.
Speaker A: Zara, tell me about your family.
Speaker B: I am having one brother and one sister.
Speaker A: 'I am having' nahi, 'I have one brother and one sister' hota hai. Having tab lagate hain jab kuch abhi ho raha ho. Jaise 'I am having tea'. Brother tea nahi hai jo abhi ho raha hai. ['I am having' is incorrect, it should be 'I have one brother and one sister'. 'Having' is used for ongoing actions, like 'I am having tea'. A brother is not tea that is happening right now.]
Speaker B: [laughs] Okay, okay. I have one brother and one sister.
Speaker A: Good. Ab batao, kal kya kiya tumne? [Good. Now tell me, what did you do yesterday?]
Speaker B: Yesterday I didn't went to college.
Speaker A: 'Didn't went' nahi hota, 'didn't go' hota hai. Jab didn't laga diya toh baad mein simple form aayega: go, eat, sleep. 'Didn't went' matlab tumne past tense do baar laga diya. [It's not 'didn't went', it's 'didn't go'. After 'didn't', use the base form: go, eat, sleep. 'Didn't went' means you used the past tense twice.]
Speaker B: Are yaar, ye toh basic hai aur mujhe ye bhi nahi aata. Class mein sab English mein baat karte hain, main chup rehti hoon. [Oh dear, this is so basic and I don't even know this. Everyone speaks English in class, and I stay quiet.]
Speaker A: Chup isliye rehti ho kyunki darr lagta hai, galat bol dogi toh koi hasega, hai na? [You stay quiet because you're afraid that if you speak incorrectly, people will laugh, right?]
Speaker B: Haan, ek baar canteen mein friend ne pucha 'What did you eat?', maine bola 'I eated rice'. Sab hase. Tab se muh nahi kholti. [Yes, once in the canteen a friend asked 'What did you eat?', and I said 'I eated rice'. Everyone laughed. I haven't spoken since.]
Speaker A: 'Eated' nahi hota, 'I ate rice' hota hai. Eat ka past tense ate hai, irregular verb hai. Par tumhari galti nahi hai, school mein rules rataye the, samjhaye nahi the. Isliye English Seekho app banaya gaya hai. Expert ke chhote-chhote video hain, Hindi mein samjhate hain. Do-paanch minute ke lessons, bilkul aise hi jaise main samjha rahi hoon. Aur main hoon AI coach, 24 ghante available. Roz expert se seekho, mere saath aake practice karo. Tumse 500 baar galti karwaungi, har baar sudharungi. Kabhi nahi bolungi 'itna bhi nahi aata'. [It's not 'eated', it's 'I ate rice'. The past tense of eat is ate, an irregular verb. But it's not your fault; schools made you memorize rules instead of explaining them. That's why the English Seekho app was made. It has short expert videos explaining in Hindi. 2-5 minute lessons, just like I'm explaining. And I am your AI coach, available 24/7. Learn from experts daily, and practice with me. I'll let you make 500 mistakes and correct you every time without judging.]
Speaker B: Lekin time kahan hai yaar? College, tuition, ghar ka kaam... [But where is the time? College, tuition, housework...]
Speaker A: Roz sirf 15-20 minute. Jitna time reels dekhne mein jata hai. Ek mahine mein farq dikhne lagega. Aur trial sirf ek rupee ka hai, canteen ki chai se bhi sasta. Install ka button dabao aur English Seekho app download karo. Ek mahine baad jab canteen mein confidently bologe 'I ate rice', tab samajh aayega asli farq. Aur jo hase those na, wahi puchenge 'teri English achhi kaise ho gayi?'. [Just 15-20 minutes daily, the same time spent watching reels. You'll see a difference in a month. And the trial is just 1 rupee, cheaper than canteen tea. Tap install and download English Seekho. In a month, when you confidently say 'I ate rice' in the canteen, you'll see the real difference. And those who laughed will ask how your English got so good.]
Speaker C (Voiceover): Install button pe click karo aur English Seekho app download karo. [Click the install button and download the English Seekho app.]
